question.problem:
Suppose we wish to find a critical point of the function $f(x,y)$ in the region $[1,2]\times [1,2]⊆{R}^{2},$ where $$ f(x,y)=3x{y}^{2}+3{x}^{2}-8xy-x. $$ Calculate one iteration of the Newton-Raphson process for optimization that starts at ${x}_{0}=[1,\,1]^{T}.$ Round your final answer to **three decimal places.**
${x}_{1}=[$ {{field-1}} $]$
{{field-2}}
question.worked_solution:
The Newton-Raphson method of optimizing a multivariable function $f:{R}^{n}\to R$ is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-[{H}_{f}({x}_{n})]^{-1}∇f({x}_{n}),
$$

where $H({x}_{n})$ and $∇f({x}_{n})$ are the Hessian and gradient of $f$, respectively, evaluated at ${x}_{n}.$

In our case, the gradient is

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}(3x{y}^{2}+3{x}^{2}-8xy-x) \\ \frac{∂}{∂y}(3x{y}^{2}+3{x}^{2}-8xy-x)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3{y}^{2}+6x-8y-1 \\ 6xy-8x\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

and the Hessian is

$$
\begin{aligned}{H}_{f}(x) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}(3{y}^{2}+6x-8y-1) & \frac{∂}{∂x}(6xy-8x) \\ \frac{∂}{∂y}(3{y}^{2}+6x-8y-1) & \frac{∂}{∂y}(6xy-8x)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}6 & 6y-8 \\ 6y-8 & 6x\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson formula is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-{[\begin{aligned}6 & 6y-8 \\ 6y-8 & 6x\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}3{y}^{2}+6x-8y-1 \\ 6xy-8x\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}.
$$

Starting with
${x}_{0}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & ={x}_{0}-{[\begin{aligned}6 & 6y-8 \\ 6y-8 & 6x\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{0}}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}3{y}^{2}+6x-8y-1 \\ 6xy-8x\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{0}} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]-{[\begin{aligned}6 & 6(1)-8 \\ 6(1)-8 & 6(1)\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}3(1)^{2}+6(1)-8(1)-1 \\ 6(1)(1)-8(1)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]-{[\begin{aligned}6 & -2 \\ -2 & 6\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]-\frac{1}{6\cdot 6-(-2)\cdot (-2)}[\begin{aligned}6 & 2 \\ 2 & 6\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]-\frac{1}{32}[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ -12\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1.125 \\ 1.375\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
